title: Doom Pilgrim: Doom Deeper - a look at these awesome new expansions
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FAIITnGT4wo

Daniel (@dungeondive) returns to Doom Pilgrim, Wacław Tryjer's card-based solo adventure, to survey everything that has appeared around it. He describes the base game as a Fighting Fantasy gamebook rebuilt as cards, with almost no mechanisms — no dice, no challenges to overcome. You pick one card from a spread by its art, read what befalls you, and track keywords, afflictions and the occasional lost limb. The comparison he reaches for is idle clicker games: you are steering a journey rather than beating it.

The headline is Doom Deeper, a review copy that splits into three eighteen-card subdecks with distinct tempers — the Futile Heavens softens the game, the Fatal Ends sharpens it, and the Pagan Echo brings heathen flavour at roughly even odds. You mix one into your chosen base deck, which he rates as the best kind of expansion because it enlarges what already exists instead of bolting on rules.

Also covered: a coffin-shaped storage box he defends at length as a portal to a contained world, a sub-ten-dollar Freak Cult dungeon, and Grimlands Adventure, a poker-sized deck of Tryjer's art with deliberately blank backs. You scout it for images that spark something, then write your own NPCs and locations onto the reverse. He calls the art the most interesting in tabletop right now, and flags the rough English translation as a real but oddly fitting flaw.

----

Daniel plans to number the blank Grimlands cards and keep their stats in a notebook rather than writing on them — is a bespoke deck better kept permanent and scrawled on, or reusable and indexed elsewhere?
